title: A Oath for the Veil
premise: Noor Thackeray, a beast-speaker in the magic-dead valley of Hollowmere, has spent a lifetime hiding the gift that would see them burned. When the old gods resume answering prayers beyond the valley's edge, Noor is dragged out of exile by a wounded godling who names them the last oath-keeper of a broken covenant. Carrying a secret that could reignite the ancient war between gods and mortals, Noor must choose between loyalty to the found family that sheltered them and the truth that could save or damn everyone. In the end, Noor breaks their own oath — speaking the secret aloud to gods and mortals alike — and shatters the covenant, forcing both sides to build something new from the ruins.
about_author: Zephyrine Nystrom is the pen name of a former court stenographer who traded transcripts of human lies for stories about divine ones. They write fantasy about oaths, outcasts, and the price of telling the truth, and live somewhere with too many crows.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. We meet Hollowmere, where magic cannot follow, and Noor's quiet double life: healer's apprentice by day, whisperer to livestock by night. When a dying crow delivers an impossible message — a god's name spoken in a dead tongue — Noor realizes the valley's protection is failing. Emotional beat: dread wrapped in longing; Noor has always wanted more, and now 'more' has teeth.

chapters.title: What the River Kept
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Following the crow upstream, Noor finds a godling washed ashore — Vess, small and wounded, half-drowned in mortal form. Vess recognizes Noor's gift on sight and names them oath-keeper of a covenant Noor never knew they inherited through their grandmother's bloodline. Emotional beat: vertigo; the hiding place was never a home, it was a cage someone built around a duty.

chapters.title: The Tithe of Small Gods
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. Fleeing hunters sent by the Church of the Silent Ledger, Vess explains the truth: the old gods went silent because mortals stopped paying the tithe of memory, and now that prayers are answered again, every faction wants the covenant — the ledger of all divine debts — before the others do. Emotional beat: bitter humor curdling into fear as Vess admits the covenant can start wars as easily as end them.

chapters.title: Bones for Bread
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor returns to Hollowmere to warn their found family — Maera the herbalist and the orphan children she shelters — and finds the Church already there, buying loyalty with grain and offering amnesty for 'confessed' magic-users. Noor must watch neighbors denounce each other. Emotional beat: betrayal; justice outside the law begins here, when lawful mercy proves to be a trap.

chapters.title: The Long Way Around the Law
chapters.summary: Noor and Vess's alternating POV. The pair smuggle Maera and the children out through beast-paths only Noor can negotiate, trading favors with river-spirits and a cynical wolf-matriarch. A Church inquisitor, Serah Ives, nearly catches them — then lets them go, for reasons she doesn't explain. Emotional beat: fragile trust; Noor learns loyalty is a currency spent best deliberately.

chapters.title: A Court of Crows and Ash
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. At the ruined temple-city of Karveth, the surviving old gods hold a fractious conclave. Vess presents Noor as oath-keeper, but the storm-god Odran demands the covenant be used to punish mortals en masse. Noor, forced to speak before gods for the first time, refuses — and discovers the covenant answers to their voice alone. Emotional beat: terror becoming power; corruption tempts even the righteous.

chapters.title: The Price of Silence
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Odran makes his offer: keep the covenant sealed, and the gods will protect Hollowmere forever — but the Church will burn a village a week until the ledger surfaces. Noor, holding the secret that could reignite the ancient war, must weigh silence against blood. Maera urges Noor to stay quiet; the children deserve safety over justice. Emotional beat: the crushing weight of being the only one who can choose.

chapters.title: Serah Ives, Believer
chapters.summary: Serah's POV. The inquisitor tracks Noor not to destroy the covenant but to read it — her order's founding sin was forging it, and she wants the truth published before her superiors bury her. She offers Noor an alliance built on mutual blackmail. Emotional beat: uneasy kinship between two people who chose truth over the institutions that raised them.

chapters.title: The Breaking of the Oath
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Climax at Karveth: Odran moves to seize the covenant by force, the Church arrives with armies, and Vess is gravely wounded shielding Noor. Cornered between war and silence, Noor does the unthinkable — reads the entire covenant aloud, every debt and every forgery, to gods and mortals together. The ancient war's last embers flare, then gutter, because no side can fight a war whose crimes are public. Emotional beat: sacrifice transfigured into liberation.

chapters.title: After the Ledger Closes
chapters.summary: Noor's POV, epilogue-like. The covenant is dissolved; gods must earn worship like anyone else, and the Church of the Silent Ledger fractures under its own exposed sins. Noor, offered godhood and refused it, returns to a changed Hollowmere — walls down, magic seeping gently in — with Vess convalescing in the barn and Maera grudgingly planting new herbs. Emotional beat: hard-won peace; the valley forgets no longer, and neither does Noor.
